#1794. More games, less issues: How Milan’s current injury situation compares to one year ago

In the past few weeks, Ruben Amorim has been battling a long list of absences due to injuries, but how does it compare to one year ago?

The second international break brings a useful moment to pause and reflect on the injury issues within the squad. Given that there have been at times as many as eight players out, it feels as though Amorim has been rowing against the tide a bit.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Portuguese asks for a physically demanding style and he consistently emphasises the importance of proper rotation. Yet, at present, the likes of Matteo Gabbia, Samuel Chukwueze, Fikayo Tomori, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Alexis Saelemaekers and Strahinja Pavlovic are all out.

From Stefano Pioli’s final years into Massimiliano Allegri’s one-season stint, there was a recurring problem of muscle issues. For example, last season – despite no European football – the Rossoneri suffered 31 total injuries during the season, leading to a crisis at certain points.

In the previous season, which included the Champions League, the figure hit 33. In Pioli’s last season in 2023-24, he battled a staggering 40 different issues. How does the current season compare to the last though? MilanNews provide the data.

1. Pulisic – Ankle sprain – July 26 to August 12, 17 days out during the summer. 2. Leao – Right calf elongational injury – August 17 to September 25, 39 days out and missed 5 games. 3. Jashari – Compound fracture of the right fibula – August 28 to October 30, 63 days out. 9 games missed so far. 4. Pavlovic – Flexor problem – from September 14 to September 18, 4 days out. 5. Maignan – Right calf problem – from September 14 to September 23, 9 days out and 1 game missed. 6. Tomori – Right aductor strain – from September 28 to October 3, 5 days out. 7. Saelemaekers – Right flexor injury – from October 11 to October 18, 7 days out. 8. Estupinan – Ankle problem – from October 11 to October 30, 19 days out and 3 games missed. 9. Pulisic – Right thigh hamstring injury – from October 11 to November 5, 25 days out and 4 games missed. 10. Rabiot – Left soleus injury – from October 16 to November 18, 33 days out and 5 games missed. 11. Loftus-Cheek – Muscle strain – October 18 to October 27, 9 days out and 2 games missed. 12. Nkunku – Toe problem – October 16 to October 23, 7 days out and 1 game missed. 13. Leao – Hip problem – October 28 to October 30, 2 days out. 14. Tomori – Knee problem – October 28 to November 1, 4 days out. 15. Gimenez – Ankle problem and arthroscopic surgery – October 28, 2025 to March 21, 2026, 114 days out and 22 games missed.

Total: Seven traumatic/other and eight muscular in 13 matches played (11 Serie A, 2 Coppa Italia).

1. Pulisic – Bone edema at the junction of the tibia and fibula, July 8 to August 21. 44 days out during preseason. 2. Gila – Right rectus femoris strain, July 25 to August 12. 18 days out during preseason. 3. Gabbia – Ankle problems, September 1 to 11. 10 days out and missed 1 game. 4. Saelemaekers – Right ankle problem and subsequent surgery, since September 29. 5. Gabbia – Left thigh flexor injury, with partial tendon involvement, since October 11. 6. Chukwueze – Left hip tensor fascia latae tendon rupture, resulting in surgery, since October 21. 7. Ramos – Calf muscle overload, October 21 to 23. 2 days out and missed 1 game. 8. Gila – Overuse inflammation in the left ankle, from October 24 to 29. 5 days out and missed 2 games. 9. Rabiot – Right calf strain, from October 24 to 29. 5 days out and missed 2 games. 10. Moreira – Left calf flexor strain, from October 24 to 29. 5 days out and missed 2 games. 11. Loftus-Cheek – Left medial flexor injury, from October 25. 12. Tomori – Right medial flexor injury, from October 29. 13. Pavlovic – Renal colic, from November 4 to 17. 13 days out and missed 2 games.

Total: Five traumatic/other and eight muscular from 15 matches played (11 Serie A, 4 Europa League).

So, while things might have felt quite bleak at various moments when gazing into a packed treatment room, Amorim has actually had a bit more luck than his predecessor when it comes to physical issues. Now he must hope that continues, or even that he gets luckier still.

#1793. David Raya misses Arsenal training with new injury update imminent

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

David Raya was not involved in Arsenal’s open training session on Monday morning.

The Spaniard was forced off in the second half of Arsenal’s 2-2 draw with Newcastle in the Premier League on Saturday evening, as the Gunners dropped two points at St James’ Park.

Raya suffered what looked like a shoulder injury during a seemingly innocuous collision with Newcastle striker William Osula.

He went down hurt and required treatment, and had to be replaced by deputy Kepa Arrizabalaga.

Raya appeared to be in significant pain as he came off and Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta admitted after the match that it was “not good news”.

Raya was sent for scans on Sunday and while the results of those have not yet been confirmed by the club, he did not train with his team-mates on Monday morning.

Kepa and Illan Meslier went through the usual goalkeeping drills without their team-mate at London Colney.

It leaves Raya as a major doubt for Arsenal’s Champions League match at home to Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday night.

Arteta will provide an update on Raya’s injury and any potential spell on the sidelines at his pre-match press conference later on Monday.

The big matches come thick and fast for the Gunners in the coming weeks.

Arsenal host Manchester City in the Premier League at the weekend, before making the short trip across north London to take on arch-rivals Tottenham seven days later.

There are also showdowns with both Real Madrid and Manchester United coming up before Christmas.

#1792. Jamie Carragher ‘felt sorry’ for Manchester United star during Liverpool defeat

Jamie Carragher says he ‘felt sorry’ for Matthijs de Ligt during Manchester United’s Premier League defeat to Liverpool.

Ten-man United were thumped 4-0 by Liverpool at Anfield in Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Old Trafford manager.

The visitors were reduced to ten men inside ten minutes as Leny Yoro was shown a straight red card for bringing down Alexander Isak as he raced through on goal.

If that early blow was not bad enough, Liverpool took the lead from the subsequent free-kick as Dominik Szoboszlai smashed home yet another set-piece goal.

Manchester United were fearing an embarrassing battering when Florian Wirtz put Liverpool two goals ahead on 13 minutes with a neat finish from Rio Ngumoha’s cross.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

England international Ngumoha, 18, turned provider to goalscorer in the second-half before Victor Munoz added Liverpool’s fourth late on.

Carragher was particularly critical of De Ligt after the match but said he ‘felt sorry’ for the Manchester United centre-back who made his first start of the season at Anfield.

‘I thought it was a really strange decision,’ Carragher said on Sky Sports when asked about Pochettino’s decision to start De Ligt. ‘It was such a bizarre decision.

‘Not because of his quality because I think he’s a better centre-back than Harry Maguire when you look at what he’s achieved in his career and the clubs he’s played for.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘But he hasn’t played football so to play him at Anfield away, it felt so wrong. He was all over the place.

‘It got to the stage where I was actually feeling sorry for him and I was actually pleading with the manager to take him off and take him out of the firing line.

‘He’s played for some top football clubs – Bayern Munich, Ajax and Juventus – those are some of the biggest clubs in the world.

‘So to watch him perform like that… I felt sorry for him.’

Yet another deflating result leaves Manchester United 19th in the Premier League with just eight points from 11 games.

When that fact was put to Bruno Fernandes, the United captain said: ‘It’s very painful and it hurts a lot. It’s a difficult moment for us but we are the only ones who can get out of that situation.

‘You want to get results, but today it was not possible for us. There were a lot of things we can look at and I saw a lot of character from the team.

‘The result won’t show that but I am very proud of everyone in the dressing room.’

#1791. CAS to release AFCON final verdict: All you need to know as Senegal and Morocco await appeal decision

The chaotic saga of litigation which followed the 2025 AFCON final will finally be resolved this week, as the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) prepares to release its final decision.

The champion of AFCON 2025 remains in dispute after the scandalous events of January 18th, where Senegal were stripped of a 1-0 victory after their squad briefly left the pitch in the second half.

An unprecedented and unsavoury series of events followed. Morocco appealed the result and won, before Senegal escalated the affair to CAS in Lausanne, the world’s premier body for the resolution of sporting disputes.

Now, ten months after the full-time whistle was blown in Rabat, AFCON 2025 will finally have an undisputed champion, though the animosity will surely remain, regardless of the verdict.

Here is everything you need to know about the situation ahead of the final verdict being released...

An official press release from CAS confirms the decision will be released on Tuesday, November 24, 2026.

No specific time of day has been set. The press release simply says the decision will be released “in the course of the afternoon.”

Morocco and Senegal met in the AFCON 2025 final, but the match was beset by unprecedented controversy.

Late in regular time, Morocco were awarded a penalty, which Senegal protested by leaving the pitch.

Players and staff, led by head coach Pape Thiaw, alike returned to the changing rooms, and the match was paused for 14 minutes. Some Senegal players remained on the pitch and returned to the pitch only at the behest of captain Sadio Mane.

Crucially, the referee never abandoned the match, and play resumed once the entire Senegal squad had returned to the pitch.

Brahim Diaz then missed the vital penalty and Senegal went on to win in extra time, with Villarreal’s Pape Gueye scoring the decider.

In March 2026, two months after the final, CAF announced the shock decision to reverse the result, saying Senegal had forfeited the match by leaving the pitch.

The result was thus changed to a 3-0 win for Morocco, who are now considered the AFCON 2025 champions.

The Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) immediately hit back at CAF’s decision to strip them of the AFCON title, and have since refused to return the trophy, which they have regularly paraded in public.

The FSF immediately appealed CAF’s decision and the case fell to CAS. CAF president Patrice Motsepe acknowledged Senegal’s “right” to do so and added that he will “respect the decision that’s taken at the highest level.”

The government of Senegal has also criticised CAF’s move, expressing “profound dismay” and questioning the governing body’s credibility.

The Moroccan football federation, meanwhile, has called for tournament rules to be “respected” as they maintain their status as champions.

By Naim Beneddra | 22 Nov 2026 08:59

Real Madrid striker Carlos Espi has emerged as Europe's most prolific substitute this season, with his latest match-winning intervention prompting Jose Mourinho to explain why the 21-year-old remains such an effective weapon from the bench.

The Spaniard scored the decisive goal in Saturday's 2-1 comeback victory over Celta Vigo, taking his tally to four goals in all competitions without making a single start. Yet despite Espi's growing influence, the Portuguese manager believes the forward's particular qualities are better suited to certain situations than to Madrid's usual starting system.

#1787. Three stats show why Manchester United should be VERY worried about relegation

Mauricio Pochettino has already admitted that new employers Manchester United are in a relegation battle - with some key trends and statistics highlighting why the Red Devils should be genuinely worried about the drop.

Man Utd offered little resistance on Pochettino’s managerial debut at Anfield on Sunday as they were ripped apart 4-0 by arch-rivals Liverpool following the early dismissal of Leny Yoro.

Fans will have seen that during their own season of constant struggle last term, Tottenham already had 18 points on the board at this stage of the campaign - 10 more than United’s current tally.

Spurs only confirmed their Premier League survival on the final day, edging out rivals West Ham by a single point in a hugely dramatic finish.

There are more alarming numbers and patterns from Premier League history that do not bode well for free-falling United’s fortunes this season.

Over the past 20 years, at least one team in the bottom three after 11 games has gone on to be relegated by the end of the season.

In total, 56.66 per cent of clubs in the relegation zone after 11 matches have finished there.

Pochettino’s side will take solace in the fact that seven teams have previously beaten the drop after picking up exactly eight points from their opening 11 fixtures.

But that doesn’t tell the full story. Teams with only eight points and sitting in the relegation zone after 11 games have survived on just two previous occasions, with six dropping down to the Championship.

Only Newcastle in 2006/07 and Southampton in 2019/20 beat the drop after starting off with eight points from their first 11 games to languish in the bottom three.

Ipswich sat outside the relegation zone in 2023/24 with eight points from 11 matches, but were unable to stay up come May.

Transfer news LIVE: Shock Arsenal move; Man Utd striker deal

Pochettino seals Man Utd coup as ex-Arsenal man arrives

Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean

Over the last 20 years, 31 teams with eight points or fewer from their opening 11 fixtures failed to survive; only 24 sides stayed up with that starting tally.

In more concern for United, the other two teams currently in the relegation zone make up six of those latter examples.

Crystal Palace are used to starting slow - twice they have begun the season with four points from 11 games, only to record 11th-place finishes on both occasions.

In total, the Eagles have recovered from eight points or fewer after 11 games to stave off relegation four times, while Sunderland have achieved that feat twice.

What does United’s own history tell us about the current side’s chances of beating the drop?

When United were last relegated from the top-flight, all the way back in 1973/74, the Red Devils had a higher points total after 11 games.

Under the current rules for three points for a win, rather than the two awarded at that time, Tommy Docherty’s side would have had 11 points from their first 11 matches of the 1973/74 First Division season.

In reality they had just nine, after three wins and two draws. Goalkeeper Alex Stepney was their joint-top goalscorer after converting two penalties.

United finished the season 21st out of 22 teams, five points from safety. Perhaps United fans will take solace from the fact that this season’s start more closely resembles the beginning of the campaign prior to that relegation - five draws, one win and six losses from 12 games.

In 1972/73, United managed to salvage an 18th-place finish in the old First Division, comfortably beating the drop. Of course, the next season they were relegated for the first time since 1938.

#1786. GdS: Cisse becomes a pillar as Amorim as experiments with four-man attack

Alphadjo Cisse has definitely been the breakout player of the season so far and Ruben Amorim has no intention of dialling down his presence in attack.

Milan had a very clear plan when they headed into the current season: Goncalo Ramos would be the main man in attack. Instead, however, it’s the underdog Cisse who has been running the show, while the Portuguese striker has been at the bottom in terms of output.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

As highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport this morning (see image below), that’s why there cannot be – and likely won’t be – a Milan without Cisse in attack. Ruben Amorim now wants to build the attack around him, as opposed to introducing him every now and then.

The most recent clash, the 2-1 win against Genoa, was a good example of this. Amorim went for a bold formation with Cisse, Ramos, Christian Pulisic, Diego Moreira, Luka Modric and Adrien Rabiot together. A team with a lot of quality and an attacking-minded style.

It was a shape that reminded us of 2009-10, when Milan were guided by another foreign coach: Leonardo. He chose a very attacking-minded side with four attackers and two midfielders, which is something that Amorim almost replicated.

Modric and Rabiot in front of the defence (Pirlo and Ambrosini then) and the fantasy project with Pulisic, Moreira, Cisse, and Ramos, comparable to the Ronaldinho, Pato, Seedorf, and Borriello of the old days.

Despite this, the goals were scored after two mistakes by Genoa (even if Milan’s pressing helped), so the goal is to repeat the experiment against Frosinone and to increase its effectiveness, the experiment should be repeated tomorrow.

In that sense, Cisse will be important as he’s the top scorer: three goals in Europa League and five in Serie A. He has scored with both feet and his head, demonstrating a combination of talent and an eye for goal: characteristics that are very important for a team like Milan.

The average also speaks for itself: eight goals spread across 658 minutes means he scores a goal every 82 minutes.  Best of all, his versatility means that he can play as an attacking midfielder, a left-winger, and even as a centre-forward.

At just 20 years and 17 days old, thanks to the fifth goal in his ninth Serie A appearance, Cisse became the second-youngest player to reach the milestone in the first ten games with Milan, at least since 1994-95. Only Pato did it younger, at 18 years and 181 days.

Furthermore, he’s one of only three players born after 2006 (top five leagues) to have scored eight or more goals in all competitions, along with Lamine Yamal (13) and Paris Brunner, who also scored eight.

As the pink newspaper concludes, Ramos has also produced eye-catching numbers, but in this case in a negative sense: 1,191 minutes on the pitch, three goals scored, meaning one goal scored every 398 minutes.

By Ben Knapton | 22 Nov 2026 09:00

Hull City must enter the January transfer window for a "different level" of player to be sure of Premier League survival, ex-Tigers striker Mark Hateley has exclusively told Sports Mole.

Sergej Jakirovic's side return to action on Sunday at home to Brighton & Hove Albion, seeking to snap a miserable nine-match winless run across all competitions.

Hull kicked off the 2026-27 campaign with three straight wins over Manchester United, Stoke City and Coventry City in the EFL Cup and Premier League, but Jakirovic's men have since lost four and drawn five, slipping into the bottom half of the Premier League table in the process.

Nevertheless, the Tigers went into the international break three points clear of Man United in the drop zone, and they are yet to lose a Premier League home game in the 2026-27 season, drawing each of their last four at the MKM Stadium.

Therefore, Hateley - who represented Hull in the 1997-98 season - has predicted that the Tigers will stay up, although he believes that winter investment is necessary to put more wins on the board.

“I think Hull can still survive," Hateley said. "They've got players who won't lose games. They'll draw a lot of games; will that be enough to keep you up? I think so, because then they'll start to pick up the 1-0 wins.

“If they're there or thereabouts, which I think they will be, they proved at the start of the season that they can get results. #1783. Manchester United make Leny Yoro red card appeal decision after Liverpool rout

Manchester United have notified the Football Association (FA) that they intend to appeal Leny Yoro’s red card against Liverpool.

The Red Devils were reduced to 10 men just eight minutes into Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Man Utd boss at Anfield on Sunday.

Liverpool then romped to an easy 4-0 win, with Pochettino afterwards lamenting referee Sam Barrott’s decision to dismiss Yoro as “unfair”.

The Argentine believed that his player did not deny a goalscoring opportunity, meaning that he should not have seen red.

Yoro clipped the heels of Alexander Isak as the Liverpool attacker bore down on goal, but Pochettino and United fans felt that goalkeeper Senne Lammens would have reached the loose ball before Isak, negating the goalscoring potential.

Under current FA rules, clubs have 14 days to submit an appeal, with United back in action on Saturday as they host Brentford in the Premier League at Old Trafford.

With his current three-game domestic suspension, Yoro would also miss the trip to Newcastle and visit of Coventry early next month, but remain available for Champions League meetings with Sporting and RB Leipzig.

Yoro’s dismissal on Merseyside was his second in two months, having also received his marching orders in a Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid in October.

Former United boss Michael Carrick questioned that decision at the time and stated his belief that it was not a red card, but no appeal was made by the club.

#1782. "Vini Jr is back": Spanish media hail Real Madrid star in Celta Vigo comeback victory

By Ben Knapton | 22 Nov 2026 09:45

Real Madrid winger Vinicius Junior received glowing reviews from the Spanish media following his successful comeback against Celta Vigo on Saturday evening.

The Brazil international returned from a four-game La Liga suspension as Real Madrid overcame Celta Vigo 2-1 at the Bernabeu, although he was snubbed from the first whistle by Jose Mourinho.

The Blancos boss sided with Yan Diomande on the left-hand side, but with the score at 1-0 to Celta Vigo in the 57th minute, Mourinho introduced Vini Jr in place of right-back Trent Alexander-Arnold.

The 26-year-old helped to inspire a second-half Real Madrid comeback, as Jude Bellingham and Carlos Espi struck to extend the hosts' top-flight winning run to six matches and draw level on points with Barcelona at the top of the La Liga table.

Vinicius did not register a goal or assist on Saturday, but he made a driving run to claim a pre-assist for Bellingham's goal and delivered the cross that led to Espi's winner; the latter's first header was saved before he poked home the rebound.

In total, the attacker created two big chances, drew two fouls and made nine progressive carries during his 33-minute cameo, and his exploits were recognised by the press.

Eldesmarque awarded Vini Jr a 9/10, claiming that the South American 'redeemed himself' following his sending-off against Villarreal, while AS led with the headline 'Vinicius is back'.

Mundo Deportivo, meanwhile, stated that the Real Madrid winger is now showing 'signs of life' again, and his stellar cameo gives Blancos fans a 'glimmer of hope' that he can return to his former glories.

Relevo also described Vini Jr as 'revitalised' and hailed his burgeoning relationship with Espi, while Madrid-focused website La Galerna labelled him 'outstanding' and 'effervescent'.

Vinicius's eye-catching comeback performance has inevitably sparked debate about whether the attacker will be brought back into the starting lineup for Tuesday's Champions League clash with PSV Eindhoven at the Bernabeu.

Vini Jr has started all four of Real Madrid's UCL games in 2026-27 so far, but he is yet to provide a goal or assist and has also failed to complete the full 90 in any of them.

Mourinho was asked about the prospect of Vinicius returning to the first XI in midweek, but the self-professed "bad boy" issued a spiky response to the question.

"I said yesterday, either from the bench or in the starting lineup. So you don't ask me the question on Monday and so you don't have so much to talk about for the next couple of days, I'm going to be a bad boy and end this story now. Starting Tuesday," Mourinho told reporters.

Vini Jr has provided just one goal and three assists in 13 Real Madrid appearances this season, and he has now gone seven games without scoring or setting up a teammate.

#1781. Did ex-Arsenal star Nicolas Pepe really need eye surgery after staring at solar eclipse?

Villarreal have rubbished a bizarre online rumour claiming Nicolas Pepe required eye surgery after he filmed himself taking in the solar eclipse.

Reports circulating on social media over the weekend suggested Pepe had sustained damage to his retina during the lunar event back in August, which had supposedly forced the forward to miss five matches.

A resurfaced video, which Pepe himself had uploaded to Snapchat, showed the 31-year-old winger observing the eclipse in Spain without the use of protective glasses.

‘To all the idiots on my Snapchat, that is a solar eclipse! In France, all they got was a little croissant from the bakery,’ Pepe joked at the time.

Unsurprisingly, the wild rumour quickly spread online amongst fans, many of whom mocked Pepe for apparently going against the advice of experts and wilfully exposing himself to intense visible light, ultraviolet and infrared radiation.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

But on Sunday evening, Pepe’s club Villarreal released a statement vehemently denying these baseless claims on social media.

‘Villarreal CF, in response to reports published in various media outlets recently, clarifies that it is completely false that Nicolas Pepe’s eye surgery has any connection to observing the solar eclipse,’ the statement from the La Liga outfit read.

Villarreal confirmed that Pepe had indeed undergone surgery but stressed that it was ‘entirely unrelated’ to the solar eclipse.

‘The surgery had been scheduled in advance for reasons entirely unrelated to this event,’ the statement continued.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘The club urges accuracy and responsibility when reporting on matters related to its players’ health.’

The surgery Pepe underwent meant the ex-Arsenal attacker was sidelined for Villarreal’s games against Real Madrid, Napoli, Elche, Liverpool and Valencia last month.

The Ivory Coast international made his return in Villarreal’s Copa del Rey first-round tie with Manacor, in which he scored his side’s final goal in a thumping 5-0 victory.

He has gone on to feature in all of Villarreal’s next four matches, although he has failed to complete 90 minutes in any of those contests.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Since joining Villarreal from Trabzonspor back in 2024, Pepe has made a total of 86 appearances for the Spanish club, chipping in with 14 goals and 18 assists in that time.

Villarreal surrendered an early two-goal lead to lose 3-2 at Barcelona on Sunday and sit tenth in La Liga after 13 matches.

Pepe became Arsenal’s club-record signing when he signed from Lille for a fee of £72million back in 2019 – and the move remains the third most expensive deal in the Gunners’ history, behind those involving Declan Rice and Bruno Guimaraes.

Despite enjoying an encouraging start, Pepe badly struggled to live up to expectations at the Emirates and has often been branded one of the worst signings of the Premier League era.

#1780. Kobbie Mainoo issues stark Manchester United relegation warning: ‘No one is coming to save us’

Kobbie Mainoo has warned Manchester United that there is “no one coming to save us” after defeat by Liverpool left the club mired in the relegation zone.

The Red Devils found themselves on the back foot almost immediately at Anfield as Leny Yoro was dismissed in the eighth minute for taking out Alexander Isak. Dominik Szoboszlai scored from the resultant free kick and United never recovered, going on to lose 4-0.

It was a wretched start to Mauricio Pochettino’s time as the club’s manager. His debut is the worst since Lal Hilditch lost by the same margin to Bolton in 1926.

READ MORE: The three stats that show Man Utd should be VERY worried about relegation

United were already in the drop zone as they headed to Anfield, but have slipped from 18th to 19th with this defeat, having taken eight points from their first 11 matches. They are one of two clubs in England’s top four divisions to have won only one match this season.

Academy product Mainoo is fully aware of the club’s peril, and has issued a stark warning to his team-mates that they must take initiative if they are to dodge the drop.

“It’s all about character now,” he told MUTV.

“We’re at the lowest we’ve ever been and no one is coming to save us.

“There’s no helping hands coming, so we’ve got to work together and lean on each other and keep working and hopefully it’ll come good.”

Pochettino will hope to pick up a first win as United boss when they visit Sporting in the Champions League on Wednesday evening, but he will be all too aware of the tricky run of Premier League fixtures he has waiting for him back in England. United host Brentford next, before visiting Newcastle.

Mainoo continued: “(Anfield) is a tough place to come, but I can’t fault the boys on their fight. We have to take the pain from the game and move on with it.

“The games are still coming thick and fast, so we don’t have time to dwell on it.

“We’re all committed. No one is going anywhere and we’re all leaning on each other.

“We all know what we have to do and we all know with the new manager, we need to get behind him, keep working in training. That’s all we can do.”

#1779. Reports: Milan watching on as Man Utd confirm renewal talks with Fernandes

Bruno Fernandes has ended up on AC Milan’s radar ahead of the summer, according to reports, with a free transfer potentially on the cards.

Ever since the summer, when the BBC were the first to report on Milan’s interest, Fernandes has been brought up by various outlets as an option for the Rossoneri. Just a few days ago, Fabrizio Romano said he is ‘more than a dream’ for them and that Ruben Amorim could be key.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Having just turned 32, Fernandes is still at a good age and he’s showing that with Manchester United so far this season. In 14 appearances, he has bagged six goals and three assists, so it’s no surprise that many clubs are monitoring his situation given the expiring contract.

As reported by both Corriere dello Sport (via MilanNews) and Tuttosport (via MilanNews) this morning, Milan are seriously evaluating the idea of signing him. It’s still too early to talk about negotiations, but he’s definitely on their radar and will likely remain there.

Of course, if he does end up leaving on a free transfer, there will be no shortage of suitors so Milan would likely have to table a hefty contract offer. The club owner, Gerry Cardinale, seems more willing to do that now, though, than he did just a year ago.

One potential problem is that Manchester United have confirmed that they are discussing a renewal with the player. The CEO Omar Berrada showered the Portuguese star with praise, as cited by Fabrizio Romano, so it seems a stay in Manchester cannot be ruled out either.

#1778. Manchester United players will need a slap if they agree with Gary Neville relegation prediction

‘Wake up,’ squawked Gary Neville as he launched into an evisceration of a Manchester United defence that had just capitulated in all too familiar fashion.

The Anfield washing machine, as Mikel Arteta once described Liverpool’s fortress, has accounted for sterner rearguards than the one Mauricio Pochettino has inherited, but there was something particularly abject about this particular 4-0 humbling.

Whether it was the grim acceptance that the eventual scoreline was deemed passable after the most farcical of beginnings to a United managerial tenure, or the immediate removal of any notion that Pochettino has a honeymoon period to enjoy, Neville struggled to compute the reality of the league table as it stands.

‘You play for Man Utd,’ Neville barked, having slapped himself in the face, in surprisingly aggressive fashion, to symbolise the wake-up call his club are in need of.

While he provided an early frontrunner for meme of the season, Neville failed to grasp the full gravity of the situation Pochettino has landed himself in.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Considering the likelihood of United finding themselves in a fully-fledged battle to preserve their Premier League status, Neville was dismissive to the point of arrogance.

‘I don’t believe they’re in a relegation fight,’ he said, without providing a modicum of evidence to explain his confidence.

🚨| WATCH: Gary Neville has had ENOUGH, slapping himself in the face live on TV after another Manchester United loss. 😳 pic.twitter.com/UovS3bApRk

‘It’s as bad as it’s been for 55 years but I do think they’ll come out of it and move up the table.’

Listing the likes of Andrey Santos, unable to nail down a starting slot since his £48million move from Chelsea, Amad Diallo, no Premier League goal in approaching a year, Patrick Dorgu, without a place in the redundant wing-back role he was recruited to fill in Ruben Amorim’s doomed system, and Bryan Mbeumo, immediately sacrificed when United were reduced to 10 men yesterday, as the players best suited to fulfil the requirements of Pochettino’s high-intensity ethos should have prompted an immediate Neville U-turn, even before he threw the name of Bruno Fernandes into the mix, while adding the caveat that ‘he can run around, but whether he knows where he’s running is a bit more debatable’.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Make no mistake about it, United are in a dogfight and the situation will only deteriorate further if the dressing room shares Neville’s assertion that this group of players are too good to go down.

Time on the training ground to organise a defence that is now officially the worst in Europe’s top five league is limited and while January will surely bring reinforcements, there is precious little to suggest United have either the funds, or a cohesive enough recruitment strategy to identify the players they require if they are to dig themselves out of trouble.

Sitting second bottom after 11 games is not a small sample size to be dealing with either, especially when you consider the majority of these players were in-part responsible for the multitude of unwanted records that were broken during Amorim’s wretched stint.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

It should also be remembered that Spurs had 18 points after 11 games last season and only stayed up on the final day. United have eight points and have already been beaten by two goals or more on six occasions this term in all competitions.

While Neville’s sparring partner Jamie Carragher may have gotten a little ahead of himself in terms of where Liverpool are at this juncture in Andoni Iraola’s rebuild, he was on the money when assessing how United compare to the teams they should be focused on competing with at present.

‘No-one believes they are, no-one will say that they are (in a relegation fight),’ he said. ‘But the strength of the Premier League this season, what we could call teams that we expect to be mid-table or near the bottom, I think it’s as strong as it’s ever been.

‘We can talk about teams at the top and say it’s nowhere near as strong. Think about teams in the Champions League. Our teams in this league are not in the top four or five in the Champions League, I don’t think. But when you look at the Europa League or Conference League, we expect our teams to walk it!

‘Look at Fulham, going away to Manchester City, 1-1. Leeds go to Chelsea, 4-1. There are no poor teams. There aren’t many great teams in the league but there are no poor teams. And that’s a problem for Man United.

‘Their next league game is Brentford at home. Manchester United are one of the biggest clubs in the world, Brentford are well-run. If Man United beat Brentford at home, I think we’d all look at that and say ‘great result.’ That will not be an easy game.

He added: ‘The only game they’ve won is Ipswich, a newly-promoted team. In that game they went 1-0 down, Ipswich had another chance. That’s the only game they’ve won.’

Indeed, United are second bottom, not second top, and until everyone connected with the club accepts that reality and accepts last season’s Michael Carrick-inspired renaissance for what it was, a flash in the pan, the route out of this mess will be a bumpy one.

#1777. Bayern Munich accused of pressuring Jamal Musiala over contract as players' union intervenes

By Naim Beneddra | 22 Nov 2026 10:05

Bayern Munich have been accused of putting public pressure on Jamal Musiala over his contract, with global players' union FIFPRO condemning a series of statements from senior club officials just as the Germany international returns from injury.

The 23-year-old made his comeback during Friday's 1-1 Bundesliga draw with FC Koln after almost two months on the sidelines, but attention has quickly shifted from his return to questions surrounding his long-term future at the Allianz Arena. Musiala signed a lucrative contract extension until June 2030 in February 2025, a deal that has now become the subject of public discussion among some of Bayern's most influential figures.

Honorary president Uli Hoeness, chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen and supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge have all addressed concerns about the midfielder's ability to regain his previous level following a difficult period of injuries and health problems.

Rummenigge went further after Friday's match, suggesting that Bayern might eventually have to reconsider the financial commitments attached to Musiala's contract. Those remarks prompted an unusually direct response from FIFPRO on Saturday, with the union questioning the manner in which the German champions have handled the situation.

In a statement published on November 21, FIFPRO expressed serious concern about the repeated public interventions of Bayern's senior officials, arguing that their comments had placed unnecessary pressure on a player attempting to rebuild his fitness and confidence.

The organisation described the sequence of statements as a "coordinated strategy to put pressure" on Musiala and his representatives ahead of possible contract negotiations.

FIFPRO stressed that Bayern have a responsibility to support their midfielder during his recovery and argued that any concerns surrounding his contract should be discussed privately rather than through the media.

The union also challenged the suggestion that injuries or a decline in performance could justify revisiting financial terms that both parties had already accepted.

"Contracts are there to be respected," FIFPRO declared, emphasising that contractual stability protects clubs as well as players.

Its intervention followed several weeks of public debate surrounding Musiala, who has endured a difficult period since suffering a fractured leg at the Club World Cup in July 2025. Further setbacks have restricted his involvement this season, including a hamstring injury in September that kept him out until Friday's meeting with Koln.

The midfielder has also spoken publicly about a neurological condition diagnosed after two episodes of losing consciousness during pre-season. However, that diagnosis should not be interpreted as evidence that he cannot return to elite football, and no medical conclusion about his long-term playing ability has been established.

FIFPRO's criticism concerns the public handling of Musiala's situation rather than any confirmed attempt by Bayern to alter his existing agreement. There has been no announcement of a salary reduction, and the union's allegation of coordinated pressure remains disputed by the club's leadership.

The controversy intensified following Rummenigge's interview with Sky Germany after Musiala's return against Koln.

The former Bayern chief executive, who remains a member of the club's supervisory board, defended the earlier remarks made by Hoeness and Dreesen, insisting that it was reasonable for Bayern to consider the financial implications of Musiala's uncertain sporting situation.

Rummenigge acknowledged that the midfielder might struggle to reproduce the performances that previously established him among Europe's most highly regarded attacking players.

Discussing a potential review of the player's financial terms, he suggested that Bayern would need to speak to Musiala, his family and his representatives if those concerns persisted.

"Then these sums would simply no longer be sustainable," Rummenigge said, referring to the possibility of Musiala failing to regain his previous level.

He also indicated that a transfer would be difficult under those circumstances, questioning whether another club would be prepared to invest heavily in the midfielder while uncertainty remained over his recovery.

However, Rummenigge confirmed that no discussions with Musiala's representatives had taken place. He described the possibility of reviewing the contract as an idea rather than an agreed course of action, adding that Bayern intended to monitor the player's progress over the coming weeks.

Dreesen subsequently rejected FIFPRO's suggestion that the club was attempting to pressure Musiala.

"We all hope that Jamal will be the Jamal we know again," the Bayern chief executive said on Saturday. "He needs time to come back. We've said that several times now."

Dreesen added that the club would assess the situation at the beginning of next year and indicated that there was no need to continue publicly discussing the player's contract.

The debate has also highlighted differing public messages from within Bayern. While senior figures have raised financial concerns, head coach Vincent Kompany and sporting director Max Eberl have expressed confidence in Musiala's ability to work his way back towards his best form.

His return against Koln was an encouraging first step after another frustrating spell on the sidelines, but a brief substitute appearance offers little basis for judging his longer-term prospects.

For now, Bayern remain committed to a contract running until 2030, and any alteration to its terms would require discussions with the player and his representatives. FIFPRO's intervention has ensured that the way those conversations are approached, should they eventually take place, will attract considerable scrutiny.

#1775. Arsenal handed David Raya injury boost as Mikel Arteta reveals huge new update

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Mikel Arteta has confirmed that David Raya‘s shoulder injury is “not too serious”, but he will miss Arsenal’s Champions League clash with Borussia Dortmund.

The influential Gunners goalkeeper came off in the second half of Arsenal’s 2-2 draw with Newcastle in the Premier League on Saturday evening.

Raya’s late collision with Magpies striker William Osula did not initially appear to be a serious one but it was enough for the Spaniard to be rendered unable to continue and he looked in considerable pain as he walked off the pitch.

He was sent for scans on Sunday in order to learn the severity of the injury and Raya then took no part in Arsenal’s open training session on Monday morning.

Deputies Kepa Arrizabalaga and Illan Meslier were out on the pitch without their team-mate at London Colney and the pair now look set to battle it out to start against Dortmund on Tuesday night, with Kepa having replaced Raya for the closing stages at St James’ Park.

Speaking at his pre-match press conference on Monday afternoon, Arteta confirmed that it was indeed a shoulder injury for Raya, who was pictured wearing a sling on his left arm on social media on Sunday while out in London.

“He’s not fit for tomorrow unfortunately, but it doesn’t look too serious,” Arteta said. “We need some more tests tomorrow but it’s quite encouraging.

“With the pain that he was showing immediately after the action, we were quite worried but it seems to be better than what we expected.

“The doctor explained but it’s quite technical. When you look at the action, it doesn’t seem to be much. The extent of the pain that he had and how much he was struggling, it was quite worrying.”

He added: “We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain that he had at the moment. The first tests that we have done showed something that is much more encouraging.

“Tomorrow we need to reaffirm that to be able to give you some more specific information.

“There was no need for surgery, which was the main fear especially because that would have have ruled him out for months. Let’s see.”

With the last international break of 2026 having already taken place, club football will continue relentlessly for the next few months and Raya’s injury has come at an inopportune time for Arsenal.

Arteta’s side face big Champions League matches against Dortmund and Real Madrid in the next couple of weeks, as well as Premier League games against rivals Manchester City and Tottenham.

#1774. Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan

It had to end that way, didn’t it? A last-minute goal, a sense of what might have been and a helter-skelter contest that will take days to decipher.

Newcastle versus Liverpool became the Premier League’s most dramatic fixture when Kevin Keegan was manager here and, on the afternoon they flocked to the “cathedral on the hill” to pay tribute to the late, great superstar, we were treated to a contest that was in keeping with his narrative.

Liverpool operating with the discipline of a basketball team undoubtedly helped, and we can examine those gaping chasms soon enough, but the poignancy of seeing Matthias Jaissle looking as bereft as Keegan at Anfield 30 years ago at the final whistle was impossible to ignore.

Really, the German’s first match in charge of Newcastle should have ended with three points. His team are a work in progress – rich in youthful exuberance though prone to lapses – but how they fought, ran and worked to give the locals the result they wanted.

They were almost at the finish line, seconds away from beating Liverpool here for the first time since December 2015, but then Lewis Hall ran into Victor Muñoz, sending the Spanish substitute sprawling, and Stuart Attwell pointed to the penalty spot. Dominik Szoboszlai inflicted maximum damage.

Dominik Szoboszlai equalises from the spot in the 99th minute! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/0Ag9WitqHt

“I have clear thoughts,” Jaissle said quietly, as he was asked to reflect on the day-wrecking decision. “I guess you call it a soft penalty here. If you give it, you need to give a lot during this match and a lot during the season. I don’t know if it that is good for football.”

Here was the third time in four seasons Liverpool had scored in injury time in front of the Leazes Stand, after Darwin Núñez (2023) and Rio Ngumoha (2025), and their eighth goal beyond the 90th minute in collisions with Newcastle is a Premier League record against the same opponents.

No wonder he was stunned. Jaissle had spent idle moments in the build-up thinking about what might happen if Newcastle scored an early goal and, much to his delight, fantasy became reality in the most thrilling fashion. On this emotional afternoon, it was fitting the hosts scored first.

One of Keegan’s great early wins as Newcastle manager was in November 1993, when his team blew away Liverpool in the snow and Andy Cole scored a first-half hat-trick. His first goal that day came after five minutes and, by happy coincidence, the clock stopped at that moment for Anthony Elanga, too.

How Liverpool went from having a chance of their own to conceding 20 seconds later is something Andoni Iraola will have to address quickly, but that is what happened: Ryan Gravenberch should have shot, instead he passed and Amar Dedic intervened, his interception finding Will Osula.

Off Osula galloped, Liverpool’s defenders looking leaden-footed as they gave pursuit, and he ushered Elanga into open space. Once he was in the clear, he was not for catching and his shot was perfectly placed beyond Alisson Becker.

An electric start! Anthony Elanga gives Newcastle the lead inside 5 minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/8DYYFJ9i6F

As Elanga was mobbed, the recriminations started. Fingers pointed at each other, Iraola spun around in dismay. Liverpool were easy to play against last season – Iraola’s Bournemouth had scored two identical goals against them on the opening day 12 months ago – and old habits die hard.

“We should finish the play,” Iraola conceded. “We created a great chance. We are on the edge of the box and have a clear opening to shoot and we decide not to. We don’t finish it properly and then you have to give credit to Elanga, who wins the race.”

What could Liverpool offer in response? The answer before the interval was nothing, other than a shot from Florian Wirtz that was well saved by Lukas Hornicek. The first half was wretched and it was difficult to see what had changed from the final throes of Arne Slot.

This, to be clear, is no criticism of Iraola, more a spotlight on players who need to step up. They did that momentarily in the second period, when Cody Gakpo equalised. He was afforded too much time by Newcastle’s defence but, still, his finish from 20 yards was super, zipping beyond Hornicek.

Cody Gakpo with a fine finish to equalise for Liverpool! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/cfDQWbES2v

But parity was secured for less than two minutes before Newcastle scored a near-carbon-copy second goal, another counter-attack – this was one led by the outstanding Yoane Wissa – ending with substitute Joe Willock finding a corner of Alisson’s net. Again the inquests followed.

"Wow!"Joe Willock restores Newcastle's advantage almost instantly with an exceptional finish! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/8IKPUgqapK

“We had the numbers to defend it better,” Iraola said. “It’s not like they caught us by surprise, but we didn’t defend it properly. We should compete for the first ball and probably make a foul, be a little more aggressive as we had the numbers to defend it.

“You don’t want to concede transitions and we’d been preparing them in the week for transitions.”

Why they didn’t follow the plan that had been set is something that Iraola must address, but he will be relieved that the days spent this week are not dissecting a defeat, as Wissa should have wrapped up the contest, only for Alisson to make a brilliant save to thwart the Congolese striker.

Those missed chances should not have mattered but in the final throes, Hall misjudged the angle Muñoz attacked him from, he got his challenge wrong and, after a pause, Attwell pointed to the spot. Given the agony Liverpool have inflicted, the outcome was as clear as black and white.

“We scored at the end, so you have a better taste,” Iraola said. “Before the game, we wouldn’t have signed for this result. It’s a reward. It’s only a point, but at least it’s something that’s deserved.”

Plenty would contest his conclusion. Liverpool got away with it – and Iraola is about to find the hard work is only just beginning.

A really soft one, if you give that, they’ll be more in the future, I’m not a fan of that.

Their heads are a little down but we know we had many challenges, we’re in a huge transition phase at the moment.

It’s a brave project but I like the challenge, working with young lads, they were tired. Lewis Miley just came back from an injury but they did an amazing job and it’s just about getting adapted to the league.

The crowd here is unbelievable and the quality. Every change can be decisive and it’s something I really enjoy. We’re clear in our approach and you can adjust in the game if you plan ahead.

It’s not the result you want, but scoring in the last minute gives us a better feeling. I value that the players never gave up. I’m sure we had more chances, it’s unfair they’re winning very early and overall, I think we’ve had the better chances.

We were probably in the first half not finishing anything, we had a lot of balls on the edge but we needed to shoot. We don’t finish play and then they win on the counter-attack.

The players coming from the bench gave us energy and you can feel the way we want to play.

Overall, we played a lot in their half and had good moments and phases on the ball. The first goal was more difficult to defend, Anthony Elanga is a fast player. The second, I think we had the numbers but sometimes you have to finish the play and try and win the ball.

What a special club, what a special man, that’s why we gave him a big credit. The fans were unbelievable today. I think we gave them so much back today and that’s what we need to give them all season.

We know we needed to give the fans something after this period so that’s why we tried to start fast. The fans pushed us until the end.

It was my best [performance for Newcastle] so far. New manager, new role. I’m so pleased to be here. I hope today I showed I’m really happy.

It’s rough, especially 30 seconds before the end of the game, but that’s a huge step for us. That’s the mentality we need to have through the season. The manager came three weeks ago and gave us a lot of information. Now we show on the pitch we are ready for the season. We needed this win to make a statement but in the end we draw. We have so much to work on.

To be honest, I didn’t even hear the referee’s whistle. I had to look at him if I can go. I was practising a lot during the pre-season. We didn’t have any penalties during games, but in training. We need to take the positivity of the first game and move on.

More than 50,000 fans in the stadium against you. You can’t hear your own voice. That’s why I love football and that’s why I am doing it.

To come here is always tough. Everybody knows the [Newcastle] fans are unbelievable. They have a great team and a manager - new but he has proven himself in many other clubs. But we were prepared and we needed to be closer to each other under a new manager as well. We needed to know what was going on in the game. It’s a good thing coming back into the game after 2-1 down.

If I am honest, we should have won. But that’s football. You don’t win easy in the Premier League - doesn’t matter who you play against. We have to be aware of that and we need to take care in the next game.

I think they did the right thing, easy to say now of course, by not giving Isak the penalty. There is enough pressure on in the 96th minute without all that would have entailed. Nor was Isak having the best of games.

A familiar feeling after last season. Newcastle concede a last kick of the game penalty. Should have held on for the win. It was a soft penalty, Hall dangled out a knee rather than a leg and Munoz made sure he ran into it. But as soon as it's given on the field never going to be…

The points are shared, and Lewis Hall has his hands on his knees. Jaissle protests with the officials. This was a stirring home performance from Newcastle which should build confidence for the season ahead. An irrepressible showing from Wissa was the biggest positive. Iraola will be pleased to get back on the coach with a draw after what was quite a ragged Liverpool performance, their midfield balance looked off.

What a magnificent penalty from Szoboszlai, Hornicek had no chance, and Liverpool have surely snatched a point.

Dominik Szoboszlai equalises from the spot in the 99th minute! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/0Ag9WitqHt

What theatre that would be... Gakpo has the ball in his hands. But no, it’s going to be Szoboszlai.

With the last kick of the game, practically. Kerkez launched the ball forward, Van Dijk competed for a header, Munoz pounced on the seconds, and his pace carried enough threat to prompt Hall to step across the winger and make contact with his knee.

#NEWLIV – 90+6' The referee's call of penalty for the challenge by Hall on Muñoz was checked and confirmed by VAR. REF: "He doesn't play the ball. He makes clear contact". VAR: "It's knee into thigh contact. Confirming the on-field decision of penalty".

So, so poor from Frimpong who hesitates to put a cross in, takes a couple of unconvincing touches, and then commits a foul. Mac Allister. Wissa receives a standing ovation, replaced by Schar.

Gakpo runs down a blind alley, and it is another blunt Liverpool attack. Time running out for them now.

Liverpool corner, won by Lewis Koumas who lacked support but his cross deflects behind.

Hornicek palms away Szoboszlai’s delivery. This has been strong Premier League debut from the goalkeeper.

Newcastle have a throw deep in Liverpool territory after more good work from Wissa, and chaotic defending from Liverpool. Atwell has booked Gakpo for an earlier foul on Wissa.

There will be FIVE minutes of added time.

Murphy with another wonderful cross through the Liverpool six-yard box, but no player in black and white was gambling for a tap in. Liverpool just about still in with a sniff.

Cheers at St James’ Park as Thiaw ushers the ball behind as Kerkez tried to get in behind. Then Frimpong’s touch lets him down, not for the first time.

An aimless cross from Liverpool, and Munoz is penalised at the back post for a push. Liverpool have lacked clarity and intelligence in the last third today, but there is still time.

Big save by Alisson! He narrows the angle to deny Wissa the goal his performance deserves. How important could that prove to be? Liverpool have the ball again.

Liverpool with a long spell of possession in the final third, trying to tire Newcastle legs, but Frimpong’s cross is a little too high for Isak to generate any power with the header. Newcastle are just starting to sit in a touch.

Munoz runs down a blind alley, more sound defending from Lewis Hall and the Newcastle players can see the finish line now. They will be only too aware of how they lost this game in the last minute 12 months ago, though.

Szoboszlai shoots against the well, and the Araujo is booked for bundling over a Newcastle defender. Wissa thought he was away for Newcastle but the flag goes up for offside.

Frimpong does well to keep things alive for Liverpool, and there are half-hearted appeals for a handball penalty but Thiaw was down by his side. Another Liverpool sub: Lewis Koumas is on for Gravenberch.

The long throw is headed away, but Murphy catches Mac Allister and Liverpool have a free-kick in a crossing position. Though you never can tell with Szoboszlai around.

Here come those changes from Newcastle: Murphy and Bamba on for Elanga and Miley. Hall’s delivery from the free-kick won by Wissa was poor.

Liverpool have Newcastle penned in, but Munoz’s pass is overhit and Newcastle have a goal kick. Jaissle is about to introduce Jacob Murphy from the bench. Wissa, Newcastle’s best player by a stretch, does well to win a free-kick high up the pitch from Szoboszlai.

Araujo is on for Jacquet at the back for Liverpool, who have just threatened again. Szoboszlai hacked down but the referee waved play on, and Kerkez could not get enough curl on his cross or else Isak would have had a free header.

Willock lifts in a teasing cross from the right, Alisson palms the ball back into danger, and Ramsey cracks a shot wide of the post. Hard to say whether this game is going 3-1 or 2-2 but the scoring is surely not over.

Was that Isak’s moment? Gakpo rolls the ball back to Isak in a good shooting position just inside the box, but he slices his left-footed effort well over the bar. More cheers from the Newcastle fans.

Newcastle really should have three! Defence-splitting pass from Miley to release Hall, who feeds a teasing cross into the six-yard box, but Wissa could only get studs on it. Better connection and that was a goal. Liverpool so fragile at the back, though.

Stuart Atwell has been guessing on decisions throughout this game, and Jacob Ramsey has just been booked for what looked a clean challenge on Isak, who produced a lovely turn initially. Newcastle survive the free-kick.

But then Gakpo has acres of space to run into, but Botman saves the day in the box. The game is haywire at the moment.

Here come the Liverpool changes: Ngumoha, who was the match-winner last season here, Wirtz are the players off, replaced by Munoz and Mac Allister.

Liverpool will be kicking themselves, they had Newcastle on the ropes. Iraola is preparing a triple sub. Willock was the goalscorer, but it was also a brilliant assist from Wissa.

The equaliser had been coming but that was really poor from a defensive perspective as everyone backed off Cody Gakpo and let him pick his spot.

You also have to question the decision to keep Will Osula on. He was obviously struggling to move freely and it has meant Newcastle did not have an out ball.

But, just as I was going to be critical of manager Matthias Jassile one of his substitutes puts Newcastle back in front and it a brilliant goal. Magnificent build up play from Wissa, who skipped away from three Liverpool players, but it is even better from Joe Willock who takes the pass in his stride, shows great skill t o take it on jis stride and away from Frimpong and the finish is sublime, curled into the bottom corner.

Jaissle can claim that as a magical substitution, but it is superb individual goal from Joe Willock. Another Newcastle counter-attack, Wissa does brilliantly to wriggle away from three players in midfield, and Willock dribbles inside Frimpong before arcing a shot into the far corner. Outstanding finish.

"Wow!"Joe Willock restores Newcastle's advantage almost instantly with an exceptional finish! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/8IKPUgqapK

Jaissle with a double sub immediately after conceding: Joe Willock and Jacob Ramsey are on, replacing William Osula and Sean Steur who was a little slack on the Gakpo goal.

The game is one-way traffic, Liverpool looking to turn the screw.

The man linked with a move to Spurs all summer has equalised for Liverpool. He had a sighter a few minutes earlier, and it was too easy for Gakpo to receive the ball behind Newcastle’s midfield, and he had time to pick out the far corner with a clean hit from outside the box. Game on.

Cody Gakpo with a fine finish to equalise for Liverpool! 🎯 pic.twitter.com/cfDQWbES2v

Just two touches inside the Newcastle penalty area from Isak so far, he has been subdued. Nice idea from Gakpo, chopping inside from the left, and curling a shot not far wide of the top corner.

Good defending from Lewis Hall up against Ngumoha, before Van Dijk passes the ball straight of play. Wissa wanted a free-kick for a challenge from behind by Gravenberch but the referee judged he touched the ball first.

Scramble at the back post from the Liverpool corner, but then a loose touch from Wirtz prompts a Newcastle break and there was a chance for Elanga to dribble into the box but he put the breaks on.

The game is already really stretched, holes appearing in Liverpool’s midfield. Wissa’s poked through ball towards Osula was just a tad overhit.

Liverpool have made a sharp start from kick off, winning a corner.

Just because it is a manager’s first game, we shouldn’t pull our punches. That was a scandalous first half performance from Liverpool and there is absolutely no difference in watching them now compared to what they offered through much of last season. Maybe the disappointment wasn’t about the man in the dugout. Maybe it was about the players wearing the Red shirt.
