Discover a hidden island paradise in the Indian Ocean

It is still to be decided how many of the co-host nations will qualify automatically for the tournament.

The 2035 World Cup bid has also put forward a host stadium in Northern Ireland - Belfast’s Windsor Park - and two each in Scotland and Wales. The Scottish grounds are Glasgow’s Hampden Park and Edinburgh’s Easter Road, while the Welsh pair are both in Cardiff: the Millennium Stadium and the Cardiff City Stadium.

The remaining English host stadiums are: Villa Park, The AmEx, Ashton Gate, Elland Road, Hill Dickinson Stadium, Etihad Stadium, St James' Park, the City Ground, and the Stadium of Light.

Three more stadia could be added to the bid, most notably a potential new Chelsea ground. Discussions as to the future of Stamford Bridge have been bubbling away for decades as the club’s hierarchy debate whether to redevelop the current ground, knock it down to build a new one on the current site, or move to a new site altogether.

Birmingham City’s new Powerhouse Stadium and Wrexham’s renovated Racecourse Ground could also host matches.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham welcomed the news, saying: “The world is coming to the United Kingdom. In 2035 the biggest tournament in women’s sport will be played in cities across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, bringing visitors, investment and jobs to every part of the country.

“Our players have inspired a generation of girls. In 2035 that generation will watch the best in the world play on their doorstep - and some of them will be on the pitch. But the impact of this World Cup will go much further. It will reach into communities across the country, bring more people into the game and leave a legacy that lasts long after the final whistle.”

FA CEO Mark Bullingham said: “Hosting Euro 2022 allowed us to change the game in our country, by creating a generation of aspirational role models and growing demand from women and girls to play. Hosting a World Cup would give us the chance to build on that across all four nations.”

England last hosted a World Cup in 1966, when the men’s team famously beat West Germany 4-2 in the final to seal the nation’s first major honour. The Lionesses have since become back-to-back Euros champions in 2022 and 2025, but suffered World Cup final heartbreak in 2023 when they were beaten 1-0 by Spain in Sydney.

Before the UK’s host bid for 2035 was confirmed at a special FIFA Congress, it was also revealed that a joint bid by the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica had been approved to host the 2031 World Cup.

#1752. Arsenal vs. Borussia Dortmund: Head-to-head record and past meetings

By Ben Knapton | 22 Nov 2026 11:57, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 16:25

Separated by just one point but nine places in the Champions League rankings, Arsenal and Borussia Dortmund cross paths in Tuesday's league-phase encounter at the Emirates Stadium.

The Gunners boast a marginal advantage over their German counterparts, having taken 10 points from their opening four fixtures against Napoli, Bayern Munich, Lille and Slavia Prague.

Meanwhile, Niko Kovac has guided Dortmund to victories over Real Betis, Sabah FK and Villarreal, albeit while also overseeing a dampening 1-0 defeat away to Bodo/Glimt on matchday two.

Here, Sports Mole takes an in-depth look at the head-to-head record and previous meetings between the two sides.

From eight previous Champions League meetings between Arsenal and Borussia Dortmund, the North London giants hold the bragging rights, but only just.

Indeed, the Gunners have won four of their eight head-to-heads compared to three for BVB, while only one previous encounter has ended all square.

The 2002-03 season marked the inaugural competitive meetings between Arsenal and Dortmund, who each got one over the other in the group stage; the Gunners triumphed 2-0 at Highbury as Dennis Bergkamp and Freddie Ljungberg netted in the second half, before Dortmund prevailed 2-1 at home, courtesy of a winner from future Arsenal fan favourite Tomas Rosicky.

Not until the 2011-12 season would the two teams butt heads again, but they were subsequently drawn to face each other in three of the next four Champions League group-stage campaigns.

Dortmund and Arsenal drew 1-1 at Signal Iduna Park in September 2011, but Arsene Wenger's men prevailed 2-1 at the Emirates two months later thanks to a Robin van Persie brace.

Both sides then beat each other away from home for the first time in the 2013-14 campaign, Dortmund earning a 2-1 Emirates triumph before Arsenal won 1-0 in Germany, Aaron Ramsey nodding home the only goal.

The 2014-15 campaign also saw Arsenal and Dortmund trade blows and victories, as Jurgen Klopp inspired BVB to a 2-0 success at the Westfalenstadion, before Yaya Sanogo and Alexis Sanchez sealed an identical Gunners win in North London.

Arteta captained Arsenal to victory in their November 2014 Emirates showdown, but that would prove to be the Spaniard's final senior appearance of that season, as he picked up a serious calf injury in the second half before also undergoing ankle surgery.

Nov 26, 2014: Arsenal 2-0 Borussia Dortmund (Champions League)

Sep 16, 2014: Borussia Dortmund 2-0 Arsenal (Champions League)

Nov 06, 2013: Borussia Dortmund 0-1 Arsenal (Champions League)

Oct 22, 2013: Arsenal 1-2 Borussia Dortmund (Champions League)

Nov 23, 2011: Arsenal 2-1 Borussia Dortmund (Champions League)

Sep 13, 2011: Borussia Dortmund 1-1 Arsenal (Champions League)

Oct 30, 2002: Borussia Dortmund 2-1 Arsenal (Champions League)

Sep 17, 2002: Arsenal 2-0 Borussia Dortmund (Champions League)

#1751. Man City XI vs Napoli: Confirmed team news, predicted lineup and injury latest for Champions League

Manchester City will welcome back Matheus Nunes for their Champions League clash with Napoli on Tuesday.

Enzo Maresca’s side are looking to arrest a slump that has seen them win just one of their last six matches in all competitions.

That victory came by way of a penalty shootout against Brighton in the Carabao Cup, and they were held to a surprise 1-1 draw by Fulham at the Etihad Stadium last time out.

One key man they will be without is Antoine Semenyo, who continues to be sidelined with a knee problem that is supposed to keep him out for a total of eight weeks. He could return to action just before Christmas.

As for their returners, Nunes, the versatile Portugal international, gives City another option at right-back.

He had been out with an ankle issue, but is “fine” to face Napoli.

Elsewhere, it looks likely that Maresca will keep mostly the same side, despite the disappointment last weekend.

Gianluigi Donnarumma will continue in goal despite shaky form, and Nunes could come back in at right full-back.

Marc Guehi returned from a hip problem that he saw him withdraw from the recent England international camp, and he will play alongside Ruben Dias.

Nico O’Reilly was replaced by Josko Gvardiol at the weekend, and it is a toss-up between the pair, with Maresca still undecided on his first-choice left-back.

In the engine room, big-money signing Enzo Fernandez saw himself benched in favour of Ayyoub Bouaddi on Saturday, but he could come back into the side here alongside Elliot Anderson.
